metadata.summary: World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he will "re-establish the order" over George Russell at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix after being outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate in Azerbaijan.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli vows to 're-establish the order' over George Russell at Bahrain GP in Malaysia after losing out in Azerbaijan | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kimi Antonelli vows to 're-establish the order' over George Russell at Bahrain GP in Malaysia after losing out in Azerbaijan George Russell won the Azerbaijan Grand Prix to reduce his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli's championship lead to 66 points with eight rounds remaining; watch Formula 1's return to Malaysia live on Sky Sports from Friday morning F1 as Sepang hosts the Bahrain Grand Prix Monday 28 September 2026 16:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli says that the Azerbaijan GP was 'one of those days you have to be happy with P5' but adds that he will be 'back at my level' at the Malaysian Grand Prix. World championship leader Kimi Antonelli says he will "re-establish the order" over George Russell at this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix after being outperformed by his Mercedes team-mate in Azerbaijan. Antonelli had finished ahead of Russell in five successive Grands Prix but could only manage fifth in Baku, as the Brit produced his best weekend of the season to claim victory from pole position. The result cut Antonelli's lead over his Mercedes team-mate to 66 points with eight rounds remaining. messages.text: Whyte wants Fisher after injury hell - 'I fought Itauma with a broken foot!'

metadata.summary: Dillian Whyte provided a gruesome description while explaining the agonising injury that he suffered, just weeks before his last fight against Moses Itauma.
metadata.content: Dillian Whyte was suffering from a broken foot in Moses Itauma defeat but wants to return in British battle with Johnny Fisher | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Dillian Whyte was suffering from a broken foot in Moses Itauma defeat but wants to return in British battle with Johnny Fisher Dillian Whyte has revealed that he was suffering from a broken foot in his defeat by Moses Itauma last August; Whyte fractured his foot during his training camp and then injured it again in the changing room; 'The Body Snatcher' wants to return against Johnny Fisher this year Tuesday 29 September 2026 06:16, UK Image: Dillian Whyte wants to return to the ring before the end of the year Dillian Whyte provided a gruesome description while explaining the agonising injury that he suffered, just weeks before his last fight against Moses Itauma. "It felt like someone had dropped a dumbbell on my foot," revealed Whyte when asked to put into words the pain caused by the fractured foot that he sustained in training last summer. "I was running and I felt it [my foot] and then I went to spar and I was sparring big, agile guys and someone was pressing me, I stepped back the wrong way and then it just fractured clean. "It was terrible, but we're used to pulling off miracles. We're used to fighting injured. "I made the best of the situation and had a decent camp. I felt good during fight week and really thought I would beat Moses." Dillian Whyte 'well up' for fight with Johnny Fisher

messages.text: Littler in shock first-round exit at World Grand Prix as Van Gerwen also beaten

metadata.summary: Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix as he lost out 2-1 to Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, on the same night that six-time winner Michael van Gerwen was also eliminated.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Littler in shock first-round exit as defending champion loses to Luke Woodhouse | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Littler in shock first-round exit as defending champion loses to Luke Woodhouse World No 1 Luke Littler suffers shock 2-1 defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night in Leicester as six-time champion Michael van Gerwen is also eliminated; watch day two of the World Grand Prix live on Sky Sports+ from 6pm, Tuesday Tuesday 29 September 2026 06:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Grand Prix match between Luke Littler and Luke Woodhouse Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix as he lost out 2-1 to Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, on the same night that six-time winner Michael van Gerwen was also eliminated. Littler won the first set, but was far from his best as Woodhouse spurned several chances at double to have taken the opener into a deciding leg. Woodhouse made no mistake in sets two and three, however, to see him pull off one of the biggest upsets in the hostory of the double-in, double-out tournament. messages.text: FIFA accuses European football chiefs of 'harassment' against Infantino

metadata.summary: FIFA has accused European football chiefs of "harassment" against Gianni Infantino and trying to influence the presidential election by "spreading misinformation" against him over the World Cup venture.
metadata.content: Gianni Infantino: FIFA accuses European football chiefs of 'harassment' against world governing body's president | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Gianni Infantino: FIFA accuses European football chiefs of 'harassment' against world governing body's president FIFA has accused UEFA of a "misinformation campaign" and attempting to influence the race for its presidential campaign; FIFA president Gianni Infantino will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027, with his opponents having until Nov 18 to find an alternative candidate Rob Harris Sports correspondent, Sky News Tuesday 29 September 2026 09:15, UK Image: FIFA has accused UEFA of a "misinformation campaign" and attempting to influence the race for its presidential campaign in new court documents FIFA has accused European football chiefs of "harassment" against Gianni Infantino and trying to influence the presidential election by "spreading misinformation" against him over the World Cup venture. The claims are made in a court filing in Miami by FIFA, which has been obtained by Sky News , seeking to block UEFA's request for all the evidence related to the attempt to sell shares in the World Cup to private investors , also known as the FIFA Forward Enterprise [FFE] proposal, FIFA's lawyers write: "UEFA's conduct demonstrates that its application was made in bad faith and for the purpose of harassment." messages.text: Leicestershire's points deduction for poor pitch reduced

metadata.summary: Leicestershire’s 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations in August's win over Glamorgan has been reduced to 19.
metadata.content: County Championship: Leicestershire have eight points reinstated from 27-point deduction for poor pitch blamed on Bollywood film shoot | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Leicestershire have eight points reinstated from 27-point deduction for poor pitch blamed on Bollywood film shoot Leicestershire chief executive Emma White confirms club will still appeal its deduction for the poor pitch that groundsman Callum Lewis later argued was due to a Bollywood film shoot; they will appeal against decision despite having eight points reinstated from original 27-point deduction Monday 28 September 2026 17:38, UK Image: Leicestershire were relegated following a defeat by champions Warwickshire in the last round of County Championship fixtures Leicestershire’s 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations in August's win over Glamorgan has been reduced to 19. The Foxes were relegated from Division One of the County Championship last week following an innings defeat by champions Warwickshire. Leicestershire's groundsman Callum Lewin had argued filming of an unscheduled Bollywood film - believed to be for a biopic of former India captain Sourav Ganguly - had taken place at the ground four days before the Glamorgan fixture between August 20-23, preventing the pitch from being covered for eight hours in bright sunshine and heatwave temperatures.
